tools.name: create_bin
tools.description: Create a new no-signup capture bin. Returns a live URL you can point any webhook, callback, or agent tool-callback at, plus a token to read what it captured. No account needed.

tools.name: get_requests
tools.description: Read the HTTP requests captured by a bin (method, path, query, headers, body), newest first. Set wait to block until a request arrives — ideal for 'trigger then assert' with no polling loop.

tools.name: set_response
tools.description: Configure the HTTP response a bin returns to whatever hits its URL — set a status code, content-type and body. Use it to test how your webhook sender / agent handles a 500, a specific JSON reply, etc. Omit or reset to return the default 200. Requires the bin token.

tools.name: clear_bin
tools.description: Delete all captured requests from a bin (the bin stays usable). Requires the bin token.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_bin · Private data: create_bin, set_response, clear_bin · Public sink: create_bin, set_response · Destructive: set_response, clear_bin.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_bin · Private data: create_bin, set_response, clear_bin · Public sink: create_bin, set_response · Destructive: set_response, clear_bin

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
